newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco Symphony musicians end strike.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco Symphony musicians end strike.

text.p: Musicians of the San Francisco Symphony approved a new contract on Monday, ending a nine-week strike, the musicians and the orchestra said.
The musicians said they voted 54-41 to end the 67-day strike, which led to the cancellation of 48 concerts. The first rehearsal will be on Monday night and the first concert will be on Wednesday.
"I am pleased that we can announce a new contract and an end to the strike," Nancy Bechtle, president of the San Francisco Symphony, said.
The symphony said the new three-year contract included pay raises of about 3.6 percent a year and would put the San Francisco Symphony among the top five best-paid orchestras in the United States.
The musicians, represented by Local 6 of the American Federation of Musicians, went on strike on Dec. 5, about two weeks after the previous three-year contract expired.

The musicians said their grievances were about health benefits and the scheduling of concerts, rather than pay. Musicians' spokesman Paul Shinoff said overwork had led to many of the symphony's string players suffering repetitive stress or orthopedic injuries.

Under the new contract, the musicians' minimum pay will be $1,490 a week in the first year, rising to $1,600 a week in the second half of the third year of the contract, the symphony said. Pensions were also raised.
Symphony management won a concession on one of its main demands, changing the schedule to permit two additional Sunday concerts beginning in 1998-99.
